discovery: Discovery and design of multiferroic materials with strong magnetoelectric coupling

nominees.name: Yoshinori Tokura
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and University of Tokyo, Japan

motivation: Conventional wisdom held that ferroelectricity and magnetism exclude one another: ferroelectric distortion favours empty d-shells, magnetism requires partially filled ones. The nominees overturned this belief through material design. Spaldin explained the chemical origin of the incompatibility and prescribed routes around it, launching the modern multiferroics field. Ramesh grew BiFeO3 thin films with large room-temperature polarization coexisting with antiferromagnetic order and demonstrated electric-field switching of magnetism. Tokura discovered that spin order itself can induce ferroelectricity in TbMnO3, achieving giant magnetic control of polarization, and opened the physics of spin-driven electric phenomena that later led to skyrmions. Together they established a new class of matter where electric and magnetic degrees of freedom are coupled, a striking example of materials discovery creating new fundamental physics while pointing toward ultra-low-power memory and spintronic devices.
